title: LaTeX
lead: I have written in LaTeX since my first year at university: lecture notes in Neovim, a thesis kept as a repository with releases, and my product’s documents, where the numbers come from data.

brief.whatText: Three kinds of work in one tool: notes from 2022–2025, a thesis in 2026 and Pora na Paru’s documents since September 2026.
brief.howText: I built the notes and their setup by hand: there were no agents then. The thesis and the product’s documents were made in 2026 with Claude Code: I set the structure and the rules, the tool did the typing.
brief.openText: The thesis sources and releases are on GitHub. The documents repository is private: this page shows only how it is built and pages of an invented example.

source.b1: В настоящем разделе изложена реализация веб-составляющей платформы <<ВКурсе>>. Как и для мобильных клиентов (см.~п.~\ref{subsec:impl-ios},~п.~\ref{subsec:impl-android}), проектные обоснования принятых решений и их трассировка к требованиям первой главы приведены в главе~2 и здесь не дублируются; в фокусе раздела --- технологический стек, имена ключевых файлов и компонентов в кодовой базе, конфигурация сборки и развёртывания. Веб-составляющая, в отличие от мобильных клиентов, охватывает сразу три функциональные роли --- лендинг, публичное приложение просмотра расписания и закрытый сервис администрирования; раздельная подача этих ролей соответствует разграничению, принятому в п.~\ref{subsubsec:client-components}.
source.b3: Веб-составляющая реализована как единый Next.js-проект~\cite{nextjs} версии~16.1.6 на основе App Router; целевой исполняемой средой является Node.js~20+ (контейнерная сборка использует образ \texttt{node:22-alpine}). В качестве библиотеки представления используется React~19.2.3~\cite{react}; язык разработки --- TypeScript~5~\cite{typescript} в режиме \texttt{strict}. Стилизация выполнена средствами Tailwind CSS версии~4.1.18 (используется PostCSS-плагин \texttt{@tailwindcss/\allowbreak postcss}); набор пользовательских компонентов --- shadcn/ui (около 36 компонентов в каталоге \texttt{src/\allowbreak components/\allowbreak ui}, построенных поверх примитивов Radix UI и \texttt{@base-ui/\allowbreak react}). Иконки --- \texttt{lucide-react}; шрифты --- Geist и Geist~Mono, подключаемые через \texttt{next/\allowbreak font/\allowbreak google}.
source.b4: Все три функциональные роли веб-составляющей размещены в единой структуре каталогов App Router под локализационным сегментом \texttt{src/\allowbreak app/\allowbreak [locale]} и разделены тремя \emph{маршрутными группами} (\texttt{route groups}) Next.js: \texttt{(landing)} --- маркетинговый лендинг и блог, \texttt{(schedule)} --- публичное приложение просмотра расписания, \texttt{(service)} --- закрытый сервис администрирования. Маршрутные группы обеспечивают разные корневые макеты (\texttt{layout.\allowbreak tsx}) для каждой роли при сохранении общего сегмента локали в URL.
source.b5: Локализация выполнена средствами \texttt{next-intl}~4.7.0; поддерживаются два языка интерфейса --- русский и английский, сообщения организованы трёхуровневой иерархией (\texttt{messages/\allowbreak \{en,ru\}/\allowbreak \{common,components,pages\}/\allowbreak <namespace>.json}). На стороне серверных компонентов используется \texttt{getTranslations()}, на стороне клиентских --- хук \texttt{useTranslations()}. Темизация --- через \texttt{next-themes}~0.4.6 с тремя режимами: \texttt{light}, \texttt{dark} и \texttt{system}; тема применяется добавлением класса \texttt{.dark} к корневому элементу документа и распространяется на все три функциональные роли. В отличие от мобильных клиентов, веб-составляющая работает в единой фирменной палитре без дополнительных акцентных цветовых схем (соответствующее проектное решение зафиксировано в п.~\ref{subsubsec:design-web}).

notes.name: Notes
notes.title: Formulas at the speed of a lecture
notes.p1: In my first year I started taking maths notes on a laptop: writing by hand was slow, Word could not handle formulas, and notes in Notion were not enough for me. The first attempts are lost; the repository starts with the second year.
notes.p2: The notes are written in Neovim. vimtex builds the PDF, and LuaSnip expands abbreviations as I type: <c>ff</c> becomes a fraction, <c>;e</c> an epsilon, and <c>{le}</c> the sign ⩽ that Russian texts use. The config has {all} snippets: {auto} expand by themselves, {math} work only inside formulas.
notes.p3: Below is line 259 of calculus lecture 17 (19.11.2023), retyped with the same snippets. The PDF updates when I leave insert mode and press <c>␣c</c>: the file is saved and built once.

pages.name: Pages
pages.title: {pages} pages in two years
pages.p1: The repository holds {lecturePdfs} sets of lecture notes from September 2023 to June 2025, totalling {lecturePages} pages, and {examPdfs} collections for exams and tests, totalling {examPages} pages. {figures} figures were drawn in Inkscape and placed in the PDFs with labels typeset by LaTeX itself.
pages.p2: My group prepared for exams with these notes and collections, and so did students in the years below when they reached the same subjects.
pages.p3: In the dark theme the pages are recoloured as Zathura showed them with my Catppuccin config.

origin.name: Origin
origin.title: I did not invent the method
origin.p1: Gilles Castel took notes this way: in 2019 he described how he typed mathematics lectures in Vim and drew figures for them in Inkscape. Elijan Mastnak turned it into a detailed setup guide. I spent several months building my config from their writing and looked for answers on Reddit: there were no agents to do it for me then.
origin.p2: From them, the config takes the vimtex and LuaSnip pairing, the file layout, the trigger rules and the preamble of the first notes. Mine are the colours of the boxes around definitions and theorems, the Russian names and their snippets, the lecture date from the <c>lesson</c> command, ⩽ and ⩾ instead of ≤ and ≥, and a Russian dictionary. For this setup I moved from Windows to macOS and installed Arch Linux on my home computer.
origin.p3: In my fourth year I wrote to the guide’s author, sent him screenshots of my setup and thanked him. He replied.

thesis.name: Thesis
thesis.title: Under the page lies its source
thesis.p1: I kept my graduation thesis as a repository: the text in <c>.tex</c> files, built by LuaLaTeX through latexmk, and the university’s requirements in a separate file that the preamble is checked against. The topic: “Development of client applications for VCourse, a SaaS platform for managing academic schedules”.
thesis.p2: The requirements are set once: A4, margins of 2, 2, 3 and 1 cm, 14 pt type, 1.5 spacing, a 1.25 cm indent. That is five lines, and all {thesisPages} pages take their layout from them. The bibliography follows GOST 7.0.5 and is built without BibTeX, and the title page comes from a data file.

releases.name: Releases
releases.title: Ten releases, from 3 pages to 130
releases.p1: <c>make release</c> checks that everything is committed, builds the PDF and adds a dated tag. The tag starts GitHub Actions: the PDF is built in a container with a full TeX Live and attached to the release, and the link to the latest one stays the same.
releases.p2: Each release below is a real PDF from GitHub. On 22 May the app screenshots went in: the file grew from 391 KB to 21.2 MB in one release.

documents.name: Documents
documents.title: The product’s documents are built from data
documents.p1: Pora na Paru has many documents that live longer than a week: registers of universities and colleges, overviews, policies. I decided against keeping them in Word or a tracker’s editor, and since 30 September 2026 they have lived in a LaTeX repository.
documents.p2: One class gives every document its look, and the type shows in a label, not a colour: overview, status report, policy, register, brief, agreement. Tables and numbers are never typed by hand: a document requests them from the data in <c>document.json</c>, and under every table the build prints the date the data was checked and where it came from.
documents.p3: Every document has an access level, and the build will not let a document pull in a column or a source from a more restricted level. An issued version goes into a log with the hash of its PDF: different content cannot be issued under the same number.

checks.name: Checks
checks.title: Agents collect, the build does not trust them
checks.p1: Claude Code agents compile the registers: they go through official sites and, for every fact, bring back the page address and a verbatim quote. The repository itself was also written with Claude Code: all {commits} commits.
checks.p2: An agent’s word is not taken on trust. A script fetches every page itself and looks for the quote and the value on it, a person settles anything in doubt, and only the import writes to the data.
checks.p3: LaTeX finishes without an error even when the PDF is already broken. So {gates} checks and {tests} tests guard the build: it fails on a letter the font does not have, on a line wider than its column by more than 2 pt, on an undefined reference and on a font not embedded in the PDF.
